title: However they explain it, Rome's theologians now agree the first man's immortality was supernatural
source_text: XI. Verum utcunque istam primi hominis immortalitatem explicent Scholae Romanae Theologi, in eo videntur jam omnes convenire illam dici debere supernaturalem, non vero naturalem, prout scilicet, naturale opponitur supernaturali. Id praesertim affirmat & multis argumentis probare conatur Bellarminus. lib. de Gratia primi hominis cap. 9. Et Becanus in summa Theologiae Scholasticae. tom. 1. tract. 5. cap. 4. quaest. 1.
pass_a_gloss: But however the Theologians of the Roman School explain that immortality of the first man, in this all now seem to agree, that it ought to be called supernatural, not natural, namely as natural is opposed to supernatural. This especially Bellarmine affirms and tries to prove with many arguments. Book on the Grace of the first man, chapter 9. And Becanus in the summa of Scholastic Theology, tome 1, treatise 5, chapter 4, question 1.
pass_b_english: However the theologians of the Roman school explain this immortality of the first man, they all now seem to agree on one point: it must be called supernatural, not natural, in the sense in which natural is opposed to supernatural.

Bellarmine above all affirms this and tries to prove it with many arguments (On the Grace of the First Man, chapter 9), as does Becanus (Summa of Scholastic Theology, tome 1, treatise 5, chapter 4, question 1).

lemmas.gloss: in the sense in which natural is opposed to supernatural

choices.why: The technical pair is kept; Le Blanc will distinguish senses of 'natural' in what follows.
